§ 373. (1) Acknowledgment of deed .
Clerk may take acknowledgment to deed , al-
though he isgrantee . But when he has such
an interesthis certificatemay be impeached .
Clerk in taking acknowledgment to deedand certifying same acts ministerially.
Stevenson v.Brasher,90 Ky .,23; 11 R.,799;
13 S. W. , 242 .
(2 ) Collection of license fees. Under the
revenue law of 1886 , the county clerk, and
not the county judge , was the proper person
to collectthe license fees for retailingspirit-
uous liquors, and to receivethe commission
thereon . Severance v .Kelly , 86 Ky ., 522 ; 9
R. , 708 ; 6 S. W. , 386 ; Adams v . Stephens ,
88 Ky ., 443 ; 10 R., 1031 ; 11 S. W. , 427 .
(3) Collectionof money on judgments.
Clerks of circuitcourts have no authority to
receive money upon judgments, executions
or replevinbonds, and a payment to him is
no protection to the person making it. Dur-
ant v.Gabby ,2 Met .,91; Chinn v. Mitchell,
Id ., 92 .
(4 ) Duty in issuing executions. The mere
fact that the record was lost will not relieve
the clerk from liabilityfor failure to issue
execution . He must show diligence on his
part to prevent the loss, and also to find the
record after it was lost. If the plaintiff's
attorney had possession of the record when
execution was ordered , it is a good excuse
for the clerk's failure to issue execution .
McFarland v . Burton , 89 Ky ., 294 ; 11 R. ,
499 ; 12 S. W. , 336 .
(5) Error in entering orders- taking
bonds . While it is the clerk's duty to draft
orders, necessary for the transaction of the
business of the court, they are subject to
the judge's approval, and it will be pre-
sumed that they were done under his di-
rection. Where a guardian's bond was de-
fectivelyexecuted, the judge, not the clerk
of the county court,was responsibleto the
injured person. Kinison v. Carpenter, 9
Bush , 599. See further Summers v. City,
140 Ky .,253; 130 S. W. , 1101.
(6) Liability to Auditor for taxes on
suits. The Auditor has the right to look
to the clerk for taxes on suits collected by
him , and a trustee to whom the clerk has
assigned the fees of his office,is not entitled
to receivethem . Field v. Chipley, 79 Ky .,
260 ; 2 R. , 269 .
(7 ) Liability for money deposited or paid
into court. Not the duty of the clerk to re-
ceive money deposited or paid into court,
and the sureties in his officialbond are not
liable for his failure to pay over money
thus received. Hardin v. Carrico, 3 Met .,
289 .
(8 ) Mistake in issuing execution. If the
court quash an execution because of mis-
take of the clerk in fixingthe return day ,
and a lienacquiredupon defendant'sproper-
ty is released, the clerk is not responsible
to another defendant in the execution for
loss sustained thereby . Goode v . Miller, 78
Ky ., 235 .
(9) Omission to enter judgment . Clerk is
not liable for loss of a debt by omitting to
enter judgment therefor, unless he was guilty
of gross negligence or fraud . Com . v .
Thompson , 2 Bush , 559 .
(10 ) Preservation of records. The clerk
of the circuit court must exercise such dili-
gence in the safe-keeping of records as a
prudent man would exercise when intrusted
with the custody of papers of such value .
That an attorney had taken the record
from the office under a custom to allow at-
torneys that privilege is no excuse for the
loss of the record. McFarland v . Burton ,
89 Ky ., 294 ; 11 R., 499 ; 12 S. W. , 336.

SUBDIVISION II .
Jurisdiction — General Provisions .
§ 966. Originaljurisdiction- judges conservatorsof the peace. The
circuitcourtshallbe a court of record,and shallhave originaljuris-
dictionof allmatters,both in law and equity, of which jurisdictionis
§ 966. (1) Action to compel conveyance
of land in another State . Action will lie in
thisState to compel one who holds the legal
title to land , situated in another State, to
execute a conveyance to those to whom he
may be under obligation to convey the title.
McQuerry v.Gilliland, 89 Ky ., 434; 11 R.,
656 ; 12 S. W. , 1037 .
(2) Admiralty jurisdiction. The State
courtshave jurisdictionof personalactions
by the owners of one boat against the own-
ers of another boat for damages occasioned
by a collisionon the Ohio river. Digby v .
Kenton Iron Co., 8 Bush , 166. See Stewart
v. Harry ,3 Bush ,438; Marshall v. Curtis,5
Bush ,607; Hyatt v.Reitz,4 Bush ,395; Rake
v . Owners ,6 Bush , 25 .
(3) Amount in controversy. Several de-
mands , amounting in the aggregate to more
than fiftydollars, united in the same peti-
tion willgive the circuitcourtjurisdiction,
although each debt , with its interest, is
below that sum . Bakewell v. Howell, 2
Met ., 268 ; and see Gorley v . City of Lou .,
23 R., 1782 ; 65 S. W. , 844. So of an obli-
gation for the payment of installmentsof
lessthan fiftydollarseach, enough install-
ments being due to exceed fiftydollars.
Brown v.Brown , 10 B. M. ,247. Where sev-
eralare jointlysuableon the same contracts
for separateamounts,the aggregateclaimed
against all determines the jurisdiction.
Wilde v. Haycraft, 2 Duv ., 309; and see
notes to sec.950, defining" amount in con-
troversy."
(4) Circuit courts have jurisdictionto en-
force liens and subject lands to the payment
of demands less than fiftydollars. Bush v .
Williams , 6 Bush , 405 ; Craig v . Garnett , 9

§ 1057. (1) Character or extent of juris-
diction. County courtshave limitedjuris-
diction, and derive all their powers from
some express statutory enactment . Gilbert
v .Bartlett,9 Bush , 49; Freeman v.Strong,
6 Dana ,282; 4 Bush , 210; 2 Bush ,45. But
in probating willsand granting administra-
tion,they are courtsof generaland exclu-
sive jurisdiction. Jacobs v . L. & N. R. R.,

12 R. , 629 ; 14 S. W. , 964 .
(2) Collateralattack of judgment . The
correctnessof the judgment of the county
court can not be questioned in a proceeding
in the circuitcourt to compel the county
court by mandamus to issue the bonds of the
county. Shelby County v . C. & O. R. R., 8
Bush , 209 .
(3) Continuance of session from day to
day . The power of the court to continue its
sessionfrom day to day , and make itsses-
sion only one day ,relatesto the transaction
of such business as it may lawfully do on
any of those days , and not to the transaction
of such business as the statute requires to
be done on a particularday or within a
given time. Com .v.Yarbrough,84 Ky .,496;
8 R.,483; 2 S. W. , 68. Generallythe court
may continueitssessionsfrom day to day ,
and treat the entire time it is in session as
one day , and make and sign but one adjourn-
ing order. Com . v. Howard , 99 Ky ., 542;
18 R. , 412 ; 36 S. W. , 556 .(4 ) County court is a court of record.
The county court, being a court of record,
can only speak by its record. Fletcher v .
Light, 4 Bush , 303. Though the county
court was authorized to subscribe stock to
the Kentucky River NavigationCo., thesubscriptionwas not binding, unless the
record, disconnected from any act done out
of court by any one , or in court not of rec-
ord, amounted to a perfect and complete
subscription of stock . Mercer County v .
Ky . River Navigation Co., 8 Bush , 300 .
(5) County judge constitutesthe county
court for the purpose of fillinga vacancy in
the office of the clerk of the court . Stevens
v .Wyatt , 16 В. М. , 542 .
(6) If an act authorizes a county court
with a majority of the justices to subscribe
stock to a corporation, the county judge can
make no validorder concerningthe matter.
Mercer County v.Ky .River Navigation Co.,
8 Bush , 300 .
(7) A county judge, sittingas the county
court,had no power tolay a charge upon the
county for the erectionof a new jail, cost-
ingmore than he was authorizedto impose,
for any one object or at any one term . Har-
risonCounty v.Smith,15 В. М. , 155.
(8) In general,when referenceismade to
a county court, or the action of a county
court, it is understood as a court presided
over by the county judge alone. Bowling
Green & M. R. R. Co. v. Warren County, 10
Bush , 711 .
(9 ) Opening or alteration of public road .
Application may be made to the county
judge alone,and the court of claims is bound
to levy a tax to pay the damages and costs,and may be compelled to do so. Statute
prohibitingthe county court, composed of
thejudgealone,from making an appropria-tionor chargerge on the county of any sum
exceeding $50 for any one object, does not
apply to such a case. Spencer County v .
Com .,84 Ky .,36; 8 R.,32.
(10 ) Not exclusively a judicial tribunal.
The county court, although classed in the
judiciarydepartment by the Constitution,
and possessingjudicialpowers, is not ex-
clusivelya judicialtribunal. Many other
powers not judicial are vested in this court.
Pennington v . Woolfolk , 79 Ky ., 13 ; 3 R. ,42 .
(11) Order binding a child as an appren-
tice should exhibit the facts required by law
forgiving jurisdictionto thecourt,and itis
void if itdoes not. Chaudet v. Stone, 4
Bush ,210 ; Small v . Small ,2 Bush , 45 ; Free-
man v.Strong, 6 Dana ,282; Coffeev.Watt ,
1 J. J. M. , 306 .
(12 ) Probating wills and granting admin-
istration. In matters of probating wills and
granting administration, county courts are
not courtsof specialor limited, but of gen-
eraland exclusive, jurisdiction. The action
of the court in such cases will always be
taken to be within its jurisdiction, unless
the contrary appear ; but it may be attacked
collaterally, the onus being upon the assail-
ant to show the want of jurisdiction. Jacobs

itations. Prosecutionsby the Commonwealth to recovera penaltyfor
a violationof any penal statuteor law,and an actionor procedure at

penalty. Prosecutionsfor profane swearing,cursing,or being drunk,
or Sabbath-breaking,and againstsurveyorsof publicroads, shallbe
commenced within sixmonths afterthe offenseiscommitted,and not
after. (Election laws- prosecutionsunder ,sec.1595. Gaming - prose-
cutionsfor,sec.1980.)

§ 1407. (1) Advancements — construction
of statute. Under this statute, in cases of
intestacy, total or partial, whether appli-
cable to realty or personalty, the intention
of the testator or intestate is never con-
sulted, the cardinal object of the statute
being to make those entitled equal in the
distribution of the estate . Bowles v . Win-
chester, 13 Bush , 1 .
(2) The excess of advancements received
by one heir over the other heirs does not
constitute a debt due by him to the other
heirs. Eckler v. Galbraith,12 Bush , 71.
(2a) Education- when money given for,
will be charged as an advancement . Hill v .
Hill, 122 Ky ., 681 ; 29 R., 201 ; 92 S. W. , 924 .
(3) Evidence . Statements of the donor
made prior to or simultaneous with the ad-
vancement are competent evidence , but sub-
sequent declarations unless part of the res
gesta are not . Bailey v . Barclay , 109 Ky .,

Aylor, 158 Ky .,713; 166 S. W. ,216; and see
cases cited in note (12 ).
(4 ) Intention of parent- law not affected
by . A parent or grandparent can not, by a
mere declarationof his intention, either
make that an advancement which is not
such by law , or exempt one of his children
from liabilityto account for money or prop-
erty given him with which statute makes
him chargeable . Shawhan v . Shawhan , 10
Bush , 600; Clark v. Clarke, 17 B. M. , 699;
Cleaver v . Kirk , 3 Met ., 270.

cases may be allowed those not receiving
advancements for the purpose of equalizing
the distributees. Royse v . Royse , 17 R. ,
1403 ; 34 S. W. , 1068 .
(6) Where an intestate charged some of
his children with rents as advancements,
but made no charge against one, the latter
in the settlement of the estate should be
charged with rents. 10 Bush , 600 ; and see
Boblett v.Barlow ,26 R.,1076; 83 S. W. ,145;
Garrott v. Rives , 26 R., 10 ; 80 S. W. , 519 .
(7) Maintaining or educating- exception.
The maintaining , educating or giving money
without any view to a portion or settlement
in life constitutes the only exception ; in allother cases the gift or devise must be
charged as an advancement, and in deter-
mining whether the gift or devise comes
within this exception , the chancellor must
take into consideration the character and
value of the ancestor's estate and the value
of the gift. 13 Bush , 1; and see Brannock
v . Hamilton , 9 Bush , 446 ; and note 2a .
(8) Partial intestacy. Where the testa-
tor left a large portion of his estate undis-
posed of by his will, the heirs must be made
equal out of the undevisedestate,thosehav-
ing received property being charged with
it as an advancement . Phillips v . Phillips,
93 Ky .,498; 14 R., 493; 20 S. W. , 541; Cole
v . Palmer , 1 Bush , 371 ; Miller v . Miller, 4
Bush , 482 .
(9 ) Right to dispute correctness of. In as-
certaining the advancements made to the
variousheirsthe court is not precludedby
the will from inquiring into the correct-
ness of the amounts charged as advance-
ments . Clarkson v . Clarkson , 8 Bush , 655 ;
but a devisee will not be permitted to ques-
tion the correctness of amounts charged to
him in a will under which he claims, nor to
show that, by reason of subsequent trans-
actions, the will ought in justiceto have
been changed. Grigsby v. Wilkinson, 9
Bush , 91 .
(10 ) Satisfaction of debt . An advance-
ment to a child operates to satisfy a debt
due the child if the advancement be an
amount equal to or greaterthan the debt.
Brooks v . Summers , 100 Ky ., 620; 18 R.,
1026 ; 38 S. W. , 1047 .
(11) Value of when to be estimated.Ad-
vancements are to be estimated at their
value when made , but an advancement to
be enjoyed at a future period must be
deemed to have been given or made at the
time it was made complete by the actual
possessionand enjoyment of the propertyadvanced . Stevenson v . Martin , 11 Bush ,
485; Hook v. Hook , 13 В. М. , 527; and see
Ward v . Johnson , 124 Ky ., 1 ; 30 R., 240 ;
97 S. W. , 1110 .

(1) Allotment- recognition- estoppel.The

cludespurchasers,subjectto the dower ,from

er v.McDowell . 8 Bush ,46; Buford v.Guth-
rie, 14 Bush , 677 .

by publiclystatingat salethat she would

Bush , 702; by pleading releasingher dower .
Craddock v . Tyler , 3 Bush , 360 ; and see
Merriwether v.Sebree, 2 Bush , 232.
(9 ) Exchange of lands . While a widow
can not be endowed of lands given in ex-
change, and also of the land taken in ex-
change, she may have her election. Her

ceived does not deprive her of dower in the

er, 90 Ky ., 23; 11 R., 799; 13 S. W. , 242;
Stevens v.Smith ,4 J. J. М. ,64.

not barred by a deed of husband and wife
which is set aside at the instance of credı-
tors. Dugan v.Massey ,6 Bush ,81; Lockett
v . James , 8 Bush , 28 ; Lowry v . Fisher , 2
Bush, 70; Snappv.Snapp,87 Ky.,554; 10

allottingdower. Gasaway v.Woods,9 Bush,
72; and ifit exceedsdower- rightin value,

signed. Dower was held to be assignableto

which was owned by the husband at his
death . Copeland v . Copeland , 7 Bush , 349 .
But now by statutesuch stock is personal
property .
(13) Jointurein lieuof dower . Any con-
veyance or devise of real or personal estate,
which is intendedby the grantor or devisor

right to dower . Presumption . Tevis v . Mc-
Creary,3 Met ., 151; Yancy v.Smith,2 Met .,
408; Pepper v. Thomas , 85 Ky ., 539; 9 R.,
122 ; 4 S. W. , 297 .

vents its enforcement by disposingof his

as relievesher of the contract, and entitles

Widow of husband who holds a title bond to

band holds bond for title, and dies,his widow

arsdale,6 Dana , 204; Stevens v.Smith ,4 J.
J. M. , 64 ; Bailey v . Duncan , 4 Mon. , 256 .

tation does not begin to run against her un-
til then . Williams v . Williams , 89 Kv ., 381 ;
11 R., 608 ; 12 S. W. , 760. Suit is barred
after fifteen years after the cause of action
accrued. Anderson v.Sterritt, 79 Ky ., 499;

his will before marriage, the widow need
not renounce it, as she isnot affectedby it.

dower , or if she renounces the will and has
dower allotted, her estate is not subject to
the debts of her husband . Chambers v .
Davis , 15 B. M. , 522. Where the will gives
the widow an estate during life or widow-
hood , without any devise over , her subse-
quent marriage , without renouncing the will,

renounce the will,takes the land as devisee,

testator's debt . Hinson v . Ennis , 81 Ky .,
363; 5 R., 367; and see, further, notes (8)
and (9), sec. 1702 .

1. A court of equitymay grant relieffor any such excess of in-
terest,and to thatend compel the necessarydiscoveryfrom thelender
or forbearer .

§ 2219. (1) Accounts . Interest is allow-
able, as matter of right and law , upon an
account from the time when , by contract,
it is payable, or from the time it becomes
a liquidated one , unless the parties agree
otherwise . When account considered as liq-
uidated . Henderson Cotton Mfg . Co. v .
Lowell Machine Shops, 86 Ky ., 668; 9 R.,
831; 7 S. W. , 142 ; and see Cline v . Waters ,
28 R. , 679 ; 90 S. W. , 231 ; Com . v . L. & N.
R. R., 31 R., 819; 104 S. W. , 267. Unliq.
uidated account would not at common law ,
prima facie, bear interest. Murray v . Ware ,
1 Bibb , 325. On such demands , interest is
sometimes allowedby way of damages ,when
the debtor is justly chargeable with delin-
quency ,but never when the delay is the re-
sult of the mere failure of the creditor to
pass the collection. Mosford v . Ambrose , 3
J. J. M. , 688. Unless in such case interest
or damages are claimed , no judgment will
be rendered for either. Adams Express Co.
v . Milton , 11 Bush , 49 .
(2) Agreement not to claim usury , or a re-
lease to accomplish the same object indi-
rectly, is void. The releasor has nothing to
release until he pays the usury . Browning
v . Thompson , 13 B. M. , 387 .
(3) Agreement to pay attorney's fee. A
note or billfor a specificsum ,with legalin-
terest, and providing that the debtor shall
pay an attorney's fee if sued on , was held
not to be usurious . Gaar v . Louisville Bank-
ing Co., 11 Bush, 180. But in Thomasson v .
Townsend ,10 Bush , 114, such an agreement
was held to be usurious; and see Fidelity
Trust Co. v . Ryan ,109 Ky ., 240 ; 22 R., 734 ;
58 S. W. , 610 .
(4 ) Building and loan associations can not
chargeor exactinterestin excessof sixper
cent per annum . Simpson v . Ky . Citizens
B. & L. Asso ., 19 R., 1176 ; 41 S. W. , 570 ; 101
Ky ., 496 .
(5) Cash advances . Interest should be al-
lowed as damages . Field v .Burnam ,3 Bush ,

§ 2723. Terms defined. For thepurposesofthisact,thetermsand
definitions contained therein shall be as follows :*
Mine . In thisacttheterm " mine " includestheshafts,slopes,drifts,
or inclinedplanes connected with excavations penetrating coal stratum
or strata,which excavations are ventilatedby one general air current,
or divisionthereof,and connectedby one generalsystem of mine rail-
roads over which coalmay be deliveredto one or more pointsoutside
the mine .
The provisionsof thisact shallnot apply to any mine employing
less than six persons insidethe mine at one time.
Excavations and Workings . The term " excavationsand workings"
includesallthe excavatedportionsof a mine,thoseabandoned as well
as the placesactuallybeing worked ; also allunderground workings
and shafts, slopes,tunnelsand other openings in the course of being
sunk or driven, togetherwith allroads, appliances, machinery, and
material connected with the same below the surface .
Shaft. The term " shaft" means a verticalopening through the
stratathatisor may be used for the purpose of ventilationor drain-
age, or for hoistingmen or material,or both, in connectionwith the
mining of coal.
Slope. The term " slope" means an inclinedopening used for the
same purpose as a shaft.
Drift. The term " drift" means an opening through the strata, on
which opening the grades are such as to permit the coalto be hauled
by mules or mechanical tractionpower , and which opening may be
used forthepurpose ofventilation,drainage,ingress,egress,and other
purposes in connection with the mining of coal.

individualoperatingany coalmine,or any partthereof.
Superintendent.-The term " superintendent" means thepersonwho
shallhave , on behalf of the operator,immediate supervision of one or
more mines .
Mine Foreman .-The term " mine foreman " means the person whom
the operatoror superintendentshallplacein charge of theworkings of
the mine and of the persons employed therein. He is requiredto be
licensedor certificated,and ischarged with theduty of preservingthe
safety and health of the persons employed in and about the mine .

operatoror superintendentisrequiredto employ in the eventcertain
